lesson_title: Paper 2 Practice Run: the Rider Decoded
hook_text: One tangent line, two chords, and 6 marks fall in three moves. The tan-chord theorem, live.
clip_script: S A T is a tangent to a circle at A, with chords A B and A C drawn to the circle. The angle between the tangent and chord A B is forty degrees; on the other side, the angle between the tangent and chord A C is sixty-five degrees. Move one: the angle in the alternate segment to angle T A B is angle A C B — forty degrees, tan chord theorem. Move two: on the other side, angle A B C equals sixty-five degrees, tan chord theorem again. Move three: the angles of triangle A B C sum to one hundred and eighty degrees, so angle B A C equals seventy-five. And the check: seventy-five plus forty plus sixty-five restores one hundred and eighty exactly.
visual_style: A minimalist circle with a tangent ruler resting against it; each move fires an arc of light from the tangent angle to its alternate-segment twin, the equal angles pulsing in matching colours until the triangle closes at 75 degrees.
mood: Puzzle-box satisfaction — three clicks and the lid opens.
pacing: Deliberate setup of the diagram, three accelerating moves, a clean snap on the 180-degree check.
call_to_action: Watch the full practice run and take the rider apart mark by mark.
